title: Effects of Different Bone Substitutes on Reactive Oxygen Species Release in Leukocytes in Vitro: A Pilot Study
authors: Nomeika D, Jasiunas A, Janužis G, Skrodenienė E, Banienė R, Juodžbalys G. Int J Oral Maxillofac Implants. 2021 May-Jun;36(3):e42-e50. doi: 10.11607/jomi.8592.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Allogeneic and alloplastic bone substitutes affect leukocytes and promote reactive oxygen species emission. Xenogeneic bone subst itute presents no leukocyte stimulation and maintains anti -inflammatory conditions. Larger bone substitute mass provokes greater oxidative stress” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
